Accounting for SMARCA4, STK11, KEAP1, and KRAS together may improve interpretation of outcomes in molecularly defined NSCLC cohorts.

SMARCA4 alterations occur within an STK11/KEAP1-rich genomic context and therefore provide an important covariate framework for STK11-focused work. The study separates mutation class from protein phenotype and adjusts survival models for major co-alterations. However, retrospective treatment exposure, incomplete tissue availability, and the absence of randomized interaction testing preclude a definitive predictive claim.

Genomic enrichment, predicted variant effect, allelic loss, and IHC loss describe different layers of biology, while treatment associations arise from retrospective cohorts. The data therefore support covariate-aware hypothesis generation but not a standalone ATM- or STK11-directed immunotherapy rule.

The study triangulates genomic, clinical, and perturbational evidence but does not make those evidence layers interchangeable. KRAS stratification exposes context-specific ATM/STK11 relationships; retrospective cohorts generate a combination-therapy hypothesis; and isogenic experiments support pathway modulation rather than broad drug sensitivity. Future STK11-focused analyses should preserve these distinctions and test treatment interactions prospectively.

This study provides a direct framework for expanding an STK11 manuscript beyond sequence mutations. Its principal strength is the ordered evaluation of copy-number prevalence, allelic state, downstream expression, treatment outcomes, and immune phenotype. However, the tight linkage of STK11, KEAP1, and SMARCA4 on chromosome 19p, platform-specific deletion calling, retrospective treatment exposure, and unsupplied supplementary models prevent a causal or validated predictive conclusion. The framework should guide explicit genotype definitions and analysis-set transitions while keeping mono-allelic loss, biallelic inactivation, RNA abundance, and LKB1 protein expression distinct.

For STK11-focused writing, this article offers a transferable structure rather than direct STK11 evidence. The reusable sequence is to define loss operationally, map neighboring-locus co-deletion, test orthogonal assay concordance, report outcomes in a separate clinical cohort, and examine paired progression samples. Its MTAP-specific metabolic biology and PRMT5/MAT2A hypotheses must not be imported into STK11 claims. The sparse discordant genotypes also illustrate why combined-locus risk groups should not be used to assign a gene-specific mechanism.
